ls_emailreg.description: Decide whether this LeapSpace support ticket is about email registration or an email-account issue. Read the whole conversation before deciding. Each message is labelled CUSTOMER, AGENT, or CUSTOMER (logged by agent) - the last is a note an agent typed on behalf of the customer, such as the subject of a phone call, and counts as the customer speaking. The request is often restated or corrected further down the thread. Decide on what the CUSTOMER is asking for or reporting, not on what the agent writes. Agents routinely tell customers to sign in with their email address and password, ask which email address was used, or quote the email address on file. None of that makes a ticket about email registration unless the problem the customer raises is the email address or the account registration itself. The person writing as CUSTOMER is sometimes an Elsevier colleague forwarding a request from a customer. Judge the forwarded request. Exactly one code. If two seem to fit, pick the one the customer would name themselves. Assign the single best-fitting LEAF code (e.g. LER1.1). Never return an empty code - if the ticket does not show an email-account problem, for any reason including that it shows nothing at all, the answer is Not email registration.

leapspace_contact_reason.description: Classify the reason someone contacted support about LeapSpace into exactly one of eight categories. Each category carries a Use when definition, the Strong signals to look for, and signals that must not be treated as evidence on their own. Assign the single best-fitting LEAF code (e.g. LCR3.1). Decide WHO is asking before WHAT they are asking about. If the requester is an Elsevier employee or an internal team — including when they are asking on behalf of a customer, institution or account — classify the ticket as 'Internal staff access' whatever the underlying access problem turns out to be. Only classify into one of the access categories when the person who cannot get in is the one contacting support.
